listing.name: Political Map - Sector Map Layers - KMU
listing.summary: Currently in pre-release. Requires LazyLib and LunaLib. Safe to enable mid-save, uninstalled via settings.
listing.aiSummary: Adds political map layers to the sector map and intel screens, visualizing faction presence, claims, and domination.

description:
Political Map
as the headline feature of Sector Map Layers

This is the pre-release stage intended for public testing and feedback collection.
You can try this mod early and share your experiences, so I can improve it.
Are you struggling to keep track of faction presence and growth?
Do you want to know which systems are claimed and by who before you even take the trip there?
Do you want to paint the map with your conquests?
Do you just want to see all that border gore factions in your mod list produce?
Do you want to play Bad Apple?


  
  

This mod requires LazyLib, LunaLib.
It's safe to install mid-run,
and there's a short uninstall procedure you will need to follow if you decide to keep your save after uninstalling the mod.

This mod is made compatible with Nexerelin, Fast Rendering, Random Assortment of Things.

Sector Map Layers

is an overlay for the map screen

(Tab, Q)

, the intel screen

(E, 1)

, the minimap in the bottom right corner of the screen (replaces the vanilla radar) if you have

Random Assortment of Things

installed.

Examples

Map screen. 
Intel screen. 
Random Assortment of Things minimap.

Everything is calculated and drawn off of game data, and it gets updated as the state of the sector changes. Map layers don't alter any of the data being used to draw it, making map layers

read-only

by design.

Sector examples

Vanilla. 
Lightly modded. 
Heavily modded.

How to access map layers
KMU comes with Sector Map Layers feature turned on by default. After loading a save or starting a new game, when you open the map screen or the intel screen, you'll see a new Map layers button among map filter buttons. Clicking that button or pressing (M) enables the map layer overlay and its sidebar.


Map screen.


Intel screen.

The main control interface of map layers is the collapsible

sidebar

that lists all available layers and related knobs and toggles.

Available map layers
Political Map (P)
Focuses on populated colonies (markets) and their affiliation.
Only they paint the map.Decivilised markets are treated as populated (can be disabled in settings) and aligned with Neutral faction (politically disorganised as contrasted by the Independent faction). Systems only with decivilised markets are painted in their own style (adjustable in settings).Markets with Abandoned Station condition are treated as unpopulated and produce no map paint.All non-market entities produce no map paint.
Examples

Unclaimed unpopulated systems are drawn very faintly just to show where systems touch.
Those outlines of unpopulated systems can be toggled on and off independently from populated systems,
which are always drawn even when there's no organised faction in the system (e.g. all colonies in a system are decivilised).
You can also adjust their visual style independently from faction and decivilised systems.Any given system can be painted by only a single faction, so each system draws a presence ribbon hugging its border that represents each populated colony with the color of the faction holding them. Ribbons are shortened to represent solidified control when only a single faction or alliance is present in a system, while that presence is in no violation of unconditional claims.

Examples

Presence ribbons: Samarra draws one showing 3 Hegemony markets and 1 Independent market.Expandable system tooltips provide detailed information on how each market affects the balance of power.

Examples

Tooltips list Neutral (unowned) markets.


Tooltips list markets producing no domination score.Factions holding any population centers are listed in a sortable filter. Selecting any of them spotlights their presence across the sector. Neutral is listed there alongside organised factions, so selecting it spotlights every system holding decivilised colonies.
In domination views (Factions and Alliances) solid fill represents domination, hatched fill represents presence in a system dominated by somebody else, no fill represents claims on unpopulated systems.On the Claims view all systems are painted with solid fill.
Examples

Faction filter, expanded to 2 columns, sorted by faction attitude toward the player.


Alliances view filtered by the Luddic Church alliance.


Factions view filtered by Pirates.


Unpopulated systems get no paint in domination views.
Tia star system is shown as Hegemony-owned because Hegemony holds an unconditional claim for it.
The Political Map comes with 3 views:
Factions - paints faction territory based on a custom domination algorithm (highly customisable in settings) that weighs markets sizes, stability, whether a market is hidden, presence of an orbital station (or if a station is militarised), and the number of patrol fleets generated (by their sizes).

Examples

Luddic Church unconditionally claims Penelope's Star but isn't present there,
and per domination rules actually present faction (Independent) reads as the holder.
The claim is still listed in the tooltip.Alliances (only visible with Nexerelin installed) - same as Factions but allied factions stand as a single political entity with their holdings combined.

Examples

Tooltips in the Alliances view combine domination score of present alliance members.Claims - paints faction territory based on the vanilla system claim mechanic - dynamic or unconditional. Intel screen.

  • Focuses on populated colonies (markets) and their affiliation.
    • Only they paint the map.
    • Decivilised markets are treated as populated (can be disabled in settings) and aligned with Neutral faction (politically disorganised as contrasted by the Independent faction). Systems only with decivilised markets are painted in their own style (adjustable in settings).
    • Markets with Abandoned Station condition are treated as unpopulated and produce no map paint.
    • All non-market entities produce no map paint.

    Examples

    Those outlines of unpopulated systems can be toggled on and off independently from populated systems,
    which are always drawn even when there's no organised faction in the system (e.g. all colonies in a system are decivilised).
    You can also adjust their visual style independently from faction and decivilised systems.
  • Any given system can be painted by only a single faction, so each system draws a presence ribbon hugging its border that represents each populated colony with the color of the faction holding them. Ribbons are shortened to represent solidified control when only a single faction or alliance is present in a system, while that presence is in no violation of unconditional claims.

    Examples

    Presence ribbons: Samarra draws one showing 3 Hegemony markets and 1 Independent market.
  • Expandable system tooltips provide detailed information on how each market affects the balance of power.

    Examples

    Tooltips list Neutral (unowned) markets.


    Tooltips list markets producing no domination score.

    • In domination views (Factions and Alliances) solid fill represents domination, hatched fill represents presence in a system dominated by somebody else, no fill represents claims on unpopulated systems.
    • On the Claims view all systems are painted with solid fill.

    The claim is still listed in the tooltip.

aiDescription: Overlays the map and intel screens with layers showing faction territories, claims, and alliances based on market data. Includes a political map with views for factions, alliances, and claims, featuring presence ribbons and detailed tooltips. The mod is read-only, does not alter game data, and supports spoiler protection and compatibility with Nexerelin and other mods.
